text:
Sean Durzi came off injured reserve on Nov 22 and played 21:36 against Carolina, his first game since Oct 26. The Rangers wasted no time putting him back beside Marcus Pettersson on the second pair, and Heavy.com has already wondered whether his return forces a trade elsewhere on the blue line.

His first 14 games were a mixed bag. Two goals and five points, but New York got only 45% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about ten points worse than when he sat. The goals came on 0.5 expected, so that part was a gift.

The case for him is the puck-moving. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 89th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, and 38% of his shots came off the rush, more than double a typical defenseman.

New York is his fourth NHL team, after Los Angeles, Arizona and Utah. What to watch: whether the Rangers' second pair starts winning its minutes now that he's healthy.
